notes.title: A welcome, a trailer, and a demo - Perseverence Part 3
notes.notes:
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29115981/231783b2686b111d50fc07b4e720f6e466a7d14b.png[/img]

[h2]Hello, drama lovers![/h2]

Hope you’re having a lovely May, we certainly are. We had just released [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1367460/Perseverance_Part_2/]Part 2 of Perseverance[/url] last month and made [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/854870/Perseverance_Part_1/]Part 1 free to play[/url], [b]and we’re already back with more because we just couldn’t wait to share it with you![/b] As you may already know if you’ve watched [b]Feardemic’s Fear Fest[/b], we’ve been working on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1514460/Perseverance_Part_3/]Perseverance: Part 3[/url], and we’re finally ready to spill more tea about what’s next for Jack and Karen. 

As you may have gathered, in this one both of the main characters from the previous entries make a comeback, but, [b]here’s the twist[/b], for the first time, you get to choose which one of them you'd like to experience the story as. It’s also a culmination of a lot of work on this and previous games, so we’re really proud of what we’ve accomplished.

[b]You can read all the deets on the Perseverance: Part 3 Steam Store page or you can watch this brand new Reveal Trailer[/b] we’ve prepared just for this occasion. We’re super thrilled to share this with you, so let us know your thoughts in the comments because we love hearing from you and it gives us the motivation to keep going, and your feedback helps us create a better game. Now, without further ado, the Reveal Trailer for Perseverance: Part 3:

[previewyoutube=vLnJUUWTQ40;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Excited? Hungry for more? Well, we’ve got you covered[/b]. If you simply can’t wait to see what’s coming in the Perseverance series, you can check out the [b]FREE demo[/b] that we have just released. Simply click the Play Game button on the Perseverance: Part 3 Store Page and get right back to Grey Ville for your scheduled drama injection. [b]Oh, and while you’re on that page, don’t forget to add Part 3 to your Wishlist, to make sure you’ll never miss an update or any juicy gossip:[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1514460/Perseverance_Part_3/

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29115981/1482a96bd7d90d54abbf6625a6ad3b4ab43ccb7a.jpg[/img]

Speaking of gossip, let us know in the comments and on Twitter, whether you’re [b]#TeamJack[/b] or [b]#TeamKaren[/b], we’re excited to hear who you’ll be playing as! Make sure to tag [b]@feardemic[/b] and [b]@TitaniteNovels[/b] as well so we can see your tweets more easily. If you’d like to talk about the game and argue about which character is better, make sure to hop on [url=https://discord.gg/yTaJkdDKtY]Feardemic Discord[/url] and join the conversation there!


[b]Catch you next time, Fearfolks![/b]

notes.title: New character and UI design
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/dc748ae5f46dff6361e0c0366ec9bf68774cdd13.png[/img]
[h2][b]Hello friends,[/b][/h2]
[h3]
Some good news for you! [/h3]

[b]We have introduced a huge update to our game, which includes:[/b]
- new character design: Jack, Natalie, and Hope, who will also appear in parts two and three! (more on that later),
- A new menu and UI which introduces several new features to the game,
- All language improvements in English and French.

We moved the entire game from the Fungus tool to Naninovel. This allowed us to add many new functions to the game. 

However, there was one issue we wanted to inform you about. All your current game saves will be deleted. We are very sorry for that.

Let's start with the characters, below is a comparison with the new (right) and old design

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/d2b6223caabc04320e8c264b10d4dfcb636a1f83.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/c49a9afd289b74cff8566b8b85e88181a627882f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/1413060439a6bc6263cea408ae0313a1ec4787a6.png[/img]

Our characters appear in several emotional states: suspicious, angry, happy, neutral, sad, scared, shocked. For the graphics, we used single emotions, so the rest awaits you in the game!

                        [u]                                                                                                                [/u]

This is how the characters look in the game:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/d980b768388fb432a190ae632667984c5f54a697.png[/img]

The screenshot also shows off the new UI, which has several new features. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/6f210b0cb4dc321e7b55484ad93a6dda67f1a926.png[/img]

LOG - allows you to read all spoken dialog, choices made, or narration. It is, in other words, the history of the textual content (as seen below).

Other useful features include - auto/skip mode - which will automatically scroll the text (speed can be adjusted in options). 

Using q.save and quick loads you will be able to quickly save and load the game without having to enter the save menu.

We have also introduced a forward and backward text scrolling feature using the wheel on your mouse,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/0251206d4daec57ee67b52b9b38de3ff165f8ea8.png[/img]

Regarding proofreading, thanks to the amazing help of one of the players, Yoann, our English, and French game is completely bug-free. The whole Titanite Games team (and surely a lot of players!) are very grateful for this help. Thank you!

One last piece of information for you. The release of Part: 2 will officially take place after the Steam Festival, so in March 2022! We also officially want to let you know about Part: 3, which will be released two weeks after Part: 2! We are currently in the final stages of production.

Both parts (+ part 1) will also be released on Nintendo Switch at the same time! That's why the release of Part: 2 was postponed, because the game required a port to Nintendo Switch, and also we had to set all the release details with NS.

notes.title: Lesson one
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/ddb4f5b3bd2fd1b07c4343d575f462793c243a6f.png[/img]

[h2][b]Hello dear friends,[/b][/h2]

Over several years, we have learned to work efficiently and effectively. However, a man learns all his life, and today we would like to share with you a lesson without which today's work process would be going in a completely different (wrong) direction. 

What matters when working on any project is communication, which can sometimes be difficult. Therefore, the circulation of information is very important. What to do then? Read how the beginnings of Perseverance: Part 1 looked like.

Going back a few years - the initial vision for the game changed after six weeks of development. The first Vision Doc described a game that was ‘super-indie’. With time, many ideas came up about the game’s presentation and the amount of detail that needed to be included. We agreed on reaching a certain level of quality. But somewhere along the way, we forgot to make sure that all the artists work within the same framework. This made backgrounds and characters being imported into the project in many resolutions and sizes. Not to mention files were named in both Polish and English which made navigation around the project a hassle. Having a Technical Document with all the resolutions and sizes described straight from the beginning would save us a lot of time and errors late in the development. Moreover, such a document is a good way to introduce new people joining the team to the workflow and rules of the project. Of course, questions may always arise but Tech Doc keeps them to a minimum, and when they do arise, most of the time they are very important.

Lesson learned: always create a Technical Document, even for small projects.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/9dac60e5d2390f178b87caaf1dbb458882af56f9.gif[/img]
[i]Bob's station, from concept to finished frame[/i]

That's all for today - we just wanted to share this lesson with you :)

If you would like to stay in touch with us and be a part of our community - join our [url=https://discord.gg/D5eEzD6g7G]Discord[/url] channel.

notes.title: Creating Perseverance
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/730a2a6c4aa050b918d6ded39051fccc92420df8.png[/img]

[h2][b]Hello dear friends,[/b][/h2]

Today we're going to tell you a little bit of the story behind the creation of Perseverance.

Initially, the game's structure was supposed to be simple: a static story cutscene followed by a playable hidden object scene, followed by another static story cutscene, and so on. 

The challenge was to design the game and the story in such a way that we could 're-use' each hidden object scene at least twice. The initial story had to be reshaped. Reasons for the main character to perform hidden object tasks needed to be invented. That was a lot of work.

The first gameplay mechanics appeared. There was a huge contrast between a fast-paced story and slow-paced hidden object mechanics. We wanted the game to have a good pace, one that would engage the player.

Over time we began to see it more as a unique visual novel than the hidden objects game.

We sat down with one of our writers, and we chopped the story into five arcs. This way the number of characters and plot details that needed to be included in a single arc became countable. We began to see the full scope of a single arc, and we decided to deliver the story in episodes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/06f668e066dca1501bef9b9000dd16a5f758b27e.jpg[/img]
[i]Bob's Gas Station. 2D background for the point'n click prototype[/i]

Visual novels gameplay mechanics were easy and allowed us to focus on making the story deeper and more personal. The initial story was more about zombies and action. We managed the development of was more about the characters, their relations, and inner struggles. It was mainly thanks to my writing sidekick, Basia. She was very engaged from day one and added a lot of value to the main story. She also aided us in making the characters more believable and likable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/0bc2b5aa1eb2073045d0d328e0e5d33e0fb1b290.png[/img]
[i]Actual Bob's Gas Station from Perseverance: Part 1[/i]

We believe that failing to deliver a big game is easier than actually delivering a small one. That is why Perseverance is an episodic adventure. We are very satisfied with what we managed to achieve as a team and that Perseverance: Part 1 is worth the time to enjoy it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/05c5f394fc82151c6652f0874d7c7f0918218c60.png[/img]
[i]Actual game footage from Perseverance: Part 1[/i]

We created a game that conveys a message and lays a good foundation for future episodes.

That's all for today :)

If you would like to stay in touch with us and be a part of our community - join our [url=https://discord.gg/D5eEzD6g7G]Discord[/url] channel.

Regards,

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/db3869aeda62735eb5052695d9219d90af06d577.png[/img]

[h2][b]Hello everyone :)[/b][/h2]

We're happy that you like the new version of Perseverance: Part 1 so much. We got a lot of messages thanking us for putting so much heart into this project. We love reading these and similar things:

notes.title: Who Ellen is?
notes.notes:
[h2][b]Oh, Ellen.[/b][/h2]

[h3]If there was one character we immediately fell in love with it’s our clumsy, blonde Natalie’s co-worker - Ellen. There was something pure and innocent about her initial concept and we strongly wanted to make her part of the main plot. But how does a goodhearted, harmless person fit into a mystery horror visual novel?[/h3]

                                                       [u]                                                      [/u]

Ellen is a newcomer to Perseverance story. As a nurse, she works at the hospital - together with Natalie and other employees. She is someone who stumbles at the least expected moment - and nobody's surprised - that's just how she is. You just don’t let her handle fragile, asian porcelain. ;-)

Extremely delicate and shy, she’s like a feather in the wind. She lets life take her wherever it does... Even though she tries her best to make everyone around her feel good and is very friendly one cannot rub off a feeling of deep loneliness in her. Why would a young, beautiful woman seem so lonely?

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/bad4ba8269bf86e8ebe48777ef51a4d343b224a7.jpg[/img]

She looks happy, but is she? About 30 years old woman quickly notices that the reality is not so colorful - the job she once dreamed of is quickly becoming tired and frustrating. The stress causes her to start visiting the bar more and more often just before going to work. Hard work is one thing - but a traumatic past is another...

          [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/3bde87c076032aa64e93e99a56bfefd4a26ed348.gif[/img]

She might look happy, but is she really? Is the stress of her work pushing her to visit the local bard so often? Or is it something else? 

Ellen looks for her happiness in small pleasures and fashionable accessories: a bright lipstick, a denim jacket, colorful dresses, bandanas, and hairpins. Her appearance stands out from her colleagues. Like a child in a world of grownups: a bit passive, a bit stubborn. 
[b]
What will be her part in the upcoming Perseverance: Part 2 story? How is her relationship with Karen going to unfold? What’s her REAL story? [/b]

                                                       [u]                                                      [/u]

[b]Add Perseverance: Part 2 to your wishlist and find out on your own very soon.[/b]

Regards,

notes.title: The evolution of Karen's design
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/0df9e54aa802bc83f3a6ee73b2f3dc492571e746.png[/img]
[h2][b]Hello :)[/b][/h2]

[h3]Today let's talk a bit about our main character’s design. [/h3]

                                                       [u]                                                      [/u]

The arrival of Karen Stamp in Perseverance: Part 1 has created a strange atmosphere. A mysterious woman who is an agent, alone in a tiny town? The questions that came to light after she appeared were: [b]Who is she looking for? Who is she working for? What is her objective afterwards?[/b]

Some of these questions were answered in Part 1 while other answers are yet to be revealed. As we were working on the details for Part 2, Karen’s character has changed. Once that happened we had to rework her look. Today we are not going into the story, but into the evolution of Karen's appearance.

The gif below shows her famous debut in the first part of the Perseverance series. Black hair, red leather jacket, white shirt, black jeans, and of course, let us not forget - the cigarette. Femme fatale in all her glory.

               [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/76a08854c6b0a295be60d9866585fbd7abbbcde4.gif[/img]

                                                       [u]                                                      [/u]

Below you can see that Karen has taken shape. Her facial expressions, look details, and body characteristics - all of those are much more clear now. Finally, you can see her unique beauty and the mystery she hides.

We made sure that her design remains mostly consistent with Perseverance: Part 1. Karen still wears her short red jacket, white shirt, and black short, black hair. The one thing we did change was get rid of Karen’s sunglasses. Since most of the Perseverance: Part 2 story takes part during nighttime, it only made sense to drop this accessory.

                                                             [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/3980521792a7325691eba808f56f4f2bb9fa15c7.png[/img]
Moreover, we figured that Karen should look more ‘sharp’ and raw. We changed her facial features to fit her character better.

What do you think about "Karen's new version"? Soon you will get to know her and her story. I would forget! On our Perseverance: Part 2 Steam profile you can see some devlogs and more information about the second part of our game. There are two more posts about Karen, so be sure to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/newshub/app/1367460]check it out[/url].


[b]In closing, we have a question for you, but answer honestly :) This is just fun.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/60bd138c3e4987ffefc541181784da406fb07a91.png[/img]

notes.title: Game Development
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/5a7316dbd393bfbe11fa84e26890bfd75384deee.png[/img]
[h2][b]Hello again[/b][/h2]

[h3]Today, we want to share a bit more about the development process of Perseverance: Part 2 and what's happening behind the scenes. [/h3]
                                    [u]                                                                                                [/u]


We are really happy with how the game is taking shape! In today's devlog we're going to give a quick recap of what Perseverance: Part 2 from the other side looks like.

Let's start with some basic information:

In case you didn’t know, Perseverance is inspired by stories like “Night of the Living Dead”, “28 Days Later”, “Revival”, scandinavian crime stories such as  "The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo", and most of all – “The Walking Dead” comic series.

[b]Genre [/b]- Visual Novel
[b]Game structure[/b] - Episodic game
[b]Technology[/b] - Unity & Fungus

Have you ever wondered what the process of making a game looks like? Having many elements, they should be put together into a whole, which results in a ready-made game. Sounds banal and simple - but unfortunately, it’s a real challenge. Still, a fun one.

Getting to the point - let's take a quick look at what a typical day for our programmer looks like.

               [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/d3c98ac81bb70b3dbfbd441beb5a76f63998d86a.png[/img]
               [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/9507150ccb11ae17a416450ff7a8bc663c1fc6c5.png[/img]

To put it simply: our colleague, having access to graphic assets, the whole plot, sound files, and feature lists, combine everything into one. His task is to determine where each element should appear in the game, who says what, what will cause a given answer, or when we will hear a gunshot. In fact, he decides when the game scares you and when does it make you laugh.

Moving on, the graphics below show the process of creating a background - which (besides the story of course) is a crucial element in visual novel games.

               [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/1d5b4fb72e0dd6a97fba0dee0ee74cf8e6c20aac.png[/img]
               [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/fdb19b59a2c43f56f08792c3b0f2ef5d3a05bf31.png[/img]

Our team of talented young artists spends a lot of time on each background. First of all, we need a sketch for each background. Then there’s a 3D render, which (unfortunately) does not mean putting blocks on the screen. The process is complicated and requires finding the right camera angle, lighting, and composition.

Once our 3D artist has created the conditions and added complex 3D meshes (models), he must set the right light. In this way, the light will be reflected differently on wood and differently on stone. The goal is for you to notice what is important and to feel the atmosphere of the story.

[b]And that's it for today's Devlog. We hope you enjoyed this little peek behind the scenes![/b]

Her main task will be to track down Jane, a girl who is very important to the agency. I am sure you know who I am talking about. Karen's story is really dark and full of turning points - it will give you long and engaging gameplay.

notes.title: New allies & Part 2 reveal
notes.notes:
Dear friends,

We are happy to announce that Perseverance just got two valuable allies – Falcon Games and Ultimate Games as Steam publishers. We are more than happy to work together!

Thanks to both Falcon Games and Ultimate Games input and resources we were able to bring Perseverance: Part 1 to a wider audience and to begin pre-production for Perseverance: Part 2.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32929210/6fab82071733b03451def55c4a3b0548f627700c.jpg[/img]

We are planning an aesthetics update for Part 1 in the near future and with help from both our partners making the game even better for your enjoyment.

Stay tuned for more info!

notes.title: A short story about a peculiar visual novel
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

As we are working hard on promoting the game worldwide we have prepared a treat for those of you who are interested in game development.

Here: https://www.indiedb.com/games/perseverance/news/perseverance-part-1-is-out-now

you can find an article about the good side of working on Perseverance: Part 1. The article is not a technical one so even if you don't have knowledge on game production you should find it interesting.

Enjoy and let us know what you guys think!

notes.title: The game is here!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32929210/fec38161d595b362bdfb8b26e0b070ca08068d77.png[/img]
Dear gamers!

[b]Perseverance: Part 1 has been successfully launched on July 23rd.[/b] 

It took us a lot of effort and nerves to deliver it on time as our indie team is small but we believe that it was worth it. During last hours before launch we did some text corrections and added small bits here and there ;-) 

Please, feel free to leave your [b]reviews[/b] once you get to play the whole game. We'd love to hear from you!

[b]Enjoy![/b]

Tap It Games Team
